exposure: maternal demographic and pregnancy characteristics (e.g., age, ethnicity, antenatal care attendance)
non-adherence to established protocols (e.g., aspirin prophylaxis, antihypertensive therapy, magnesium sulphate prophylaxis)
cohort: The study included 23 Black African women with a median age of 27 years who experienced maternal deaths due to hypertensive disorders of pregnancy at a tertiary/quaternary hospital in Johannesburg between 2015 and 2018.
finding: HDP-related maternal deaths, predominantly occurring postpartum in Black African women, are largely preventable and result from poor quality of care due to a lack of adherence to evidence-based protocols.
